newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile blue chips close at lowest level in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Chile blue chips close at lowest level in 1996.

text.p: Chilean blue chip stocks sank 1.32 percent to close at their lowest point this year with the market dragged down by steep slides in electricity stocks, said traders.
The bolsa recouped some early losses on bargain hunting late in the day. This is expected to help the market regain its footing at Tuesday's opening, traders said.
"Although the underlying negative factors remain, there could be a technical rebound because of the low prices," one dealer said.
The selective IPSA index, which tumbled 2.03 percent mid-afternoon, recovered to end off 1.32 percent at 91.41 points. The general IGPA index shed 0.7 percent to 5,032.67 points.
Monday's slump brought the IPSA to its lowest point since April 8 when the market closed at 92.33 points.
Volume rose slightly to 9.9 billion pesos from 8.3 billion pesos Friday.
Traders reported heavy selling abroad of electricity stocks on fears that this year's drought will seriously hurt generating company results over the next year.
"The earnings outlook is pretty grim for 1997," said one analyst.
The drought -- the worst in 30 years -- has dried up water supplies forcing the hydro-electric companies to buy expensive power from the spot market, they said.
Recent cuts by regulators in generating prices will also hurt earnings as the rise in sales expected next year will not compensate entirely for the lower rates.
Losers included Endesa, down 2.87 percent at 223 pesos and Enersis which shed 2.15 percent to 228 pesos.
Only four stocks rose including fishing company Itata, up 5.56 percent at 95 pesos and shipping firm Vapores which gained 1.82 percent to 280 pesos.
